summary.rest: , but not by as much as your pay rise. Four things changed.
summary.source: Worked out from your March and April payslips from Meridian Payroll

rows.title: Your pay rise
rows.explain: Your salary went up by £180 a month. After 40% income tax and 2% National Insurance, £104.40 of that reaches your account.

rows.title: Cycle to work started
rows.sub: £83.33 a month for 12 months, taken before tax
rows.explain: Your bike is paid for through salary sacrifice: £83.33 comes off your pay before tax, so it only reduces your take-home by £48.33. Eleven more payments to go.

rows.title: Health cover is now taxed through payroll
rows.sub: A new line, and Sam is now covered
rows.explain: From April 2027, tax on health cover is taken through your payslip each month instead of your tax code. You’ll see “Medical benefit £116.67”: that’s the value you’re taxed on, not money paid to you. It’s higher than before because Sam joined your cover, and your tax code has gone back to 1257L.

rows.title: Pension on your higher salary
rows.sub: Still 5%, now of a bigger salary
rows.explain: You pay 5% into your pension through salary sacrifice. On your new salary that’s £9 more a month, which costs you £5.22 after tax. Meridian’s 8% grows too.

lines.label: Medical benefit (taxed, not paid to you)

questions.q: Why did my tax code change?
questions.a: Until April, the £900 value of your health cover was taken off your tax-free allowance, giving 1167L. Now that the tax is collected through payroll each month, the adjustment is gone and you’re back on 1257L.

questions.q: When do my bike payments end?
questions.a: Your last payment is in March 2028, the 12th month. After that, your take-home goes up by £48.33 a month.

flag.sent: They usually reply within 2 working days. We’ll let you know here.

march: Nothing changed in March. Your March payslip matched February’s.
